reason: The cited evidence supports that high entropy stabilizes solid solutions (E1, E2) and that lattice distortion exists (E4), but no passage provides evidence that lattice distortion reduces diffusion barriers or that a balance between entropy and distortion-driven diffusion governs stability; E3 only shows thermal stability for one composition without linking to size mismatch.
premises: High configurational entropy stabilizes a disordered solid solution at high temperatures.
Lattice distortion from atomic size mismatch enhances atomic diffusion.
Enhanced diffusion can overcome entropy stabilization, causing phase segregation or short-range ordering.
Minimal size mismatch (low distortion) limits diffusion and maintains homogeneity.
These mechanisms govern stability in HEA nanoparticles from 473–1923 K.
